name: Hunter
description:
Your traps are set in the center of the clearing, just on either side of the game trail that you know your quarry will follow. You've lain still for nearly an hour and it's about to pay off. You're downwind, so you smell them first, then hear them, then see them. Good, they are moving calmly and unwarily - they don't suspect anything. Three more steps. Two. One. You loose an arrow and it plunges deep into the leader's neck. With a scream the others scatter, running right into your traps. A series of snaps echoes off the trees and you dash from the shadows, pulling a knife across each throat quickly and silently. You come to the leader last, pulling your arrow out as the life leaves them. A tidy ambush - one of your best.

Hunters are all about care and planning. They know the land and how to use it to their advantage. The natural world is to be feared, respected and used as a tactical weapon. While they are proficient in many types of combat, they specialize in ranged weapons and trap-setting: skills sharpened in the wilderness and deadly on the battlefield.

The Hunter mestiere is part generalist, part specialist. You will have some skill with most weapons of modest make, and the Guide skill allows you to be a highly adaptive asset to your companions while traversing the wilderness. Where the Hunter truly stands apart is in their mastery of ranged weapons, especially projectile weapons like bows and crossbows. You have access to the most powerful ranged weapons in the game, and many of your abilities further amplify this specialization. Finally, you carry an array of traps that allow you to take your opponents by surprise, inhibiting their movement and dealing additional damage.

Hunter grants you broad competence to help your party gain the upper hand, then allows you to unleash some of the deadliest weapons on the battlefield.

Play a Hunter if you want to:

  • Fight from range with precision and patience, making each shot count through technique, preparation, and positioning.

  • Shape the battlefield before the first blow, using traps, poison, and terrain knowledge to set conditions that favor your party before anyone else has drawn a weapon.

  • Keep the party alive in the wild, serving as guide, scout, tracker, and forager in natural environments where your expertise is the difference between a successful journey and a disastrous one.

Questions to consider when making a Hunter:

  • What did they first learn to hunt? Do they have a quarry they consider their true calling, or are they content to pursue just about anything?

  • How did they come to their expertise? Long solitary years in the field, an apprenticeship to a master, or a community tradition?

  • What is their relationship to the places they travel through? Do they feel responsible for the land, or do they think of it as a tool?

  • How do they feel about the time their methods require? Preparation, patience, and positioning favor those who are willing to wait. Is that waiting something they find natural, or do they have to work at it?

  • Have they ever lost a quarry they were certain they had? What happened, and what did they learn from it?

novizio.description: You know how to survive in the wilderness and are skilled with the tools, traps and weapons that can keep you alive and fed.
novizio.abilities: Guide, Trapper, Set Traps and one other ability costing no more than 5 XP.
novizio.gratuiti: A waterskin, a backpack & bedroll, a traveling cloak, a hunting horn, a pocketknife.
